function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have a way to pull “live” event schedules directly into this chat—my toolkit doesn’t let me browse the web right now. However, I can point you toward reliable sources where you’ll always find an updated list of upcoming festivals in the United States, plus a quick snapshot of some big-name events that tend to happen each year.

---

### Where to Find Current Festival Listings

| Resource | What It Offers | How To Use |
|----------|-----------------|------------|
| **Eventbrite** | Search by city, state, or keyword (“music”, “food”, “cultural”) | Go to [eventbrite.com](https://www.eventbrite.com/) → use the map or filter options. |
| **Ticketmaster** | Major concerts & festivals, often sold out quickly | Visit [ticketmaster.com/events](https://www.ticketmaster.com/events) → choose your area. |
| **Local Tourism Sites** | City‑specific calendars (e.g., NYC’s “NYC Events Calendar”) | Google “[City] tourism events” – most municipal sites keep a public calendar. |
| **Wikipedia Lists** | Comprehensive lists of annual festivals per state | Search “List of festivals in <state>” or just “Festivals in the United States”. |
| **Time Out / Thrillist** | Curated guides for nightlife & culture | Check their “Events” sections for seasonal highlights. |

If you’re planning ahead, many of these platforms allow email alerts so you won’t miss tickets when they sell fast.

---

### Big Annual Festivals You Might Want to Keep An Eye On  

*(Dates vary slightly each year; check the exact dates for the current cycle.)*

| Festival | Typical Timeframe | Location | Highlights |
|---------|-------------------|-----------|-------------|
| **South By Southwest (SXSW)** | Mid‑March | Austin, TX | Music + film + interactive tech showcase. |
| **Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival** | Late April–Early May | Indio, CA | World‑famous lineup, art installations. |
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | Early June | Manchester, TN | Multi‑genre stages, craft beer tents. |
| **Burning Man** | First week of August | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art, community, self‑expression. |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | Mid‑April | New Orleans, LA | Jazz, blues, Cajun cuisine. |
| **Taste of Chicago** | July | Chicago, IL | Food trucks, live music, family fun. |
| **Pride Parade & Celebration** | Varies by city | Many cities nationwide | LGBTQ+ pride celebrations, parades, parties. |
| **Labor Day Weekend Festivities** | First Monday in September | Nationwide | State fairs, fireworks, beach bonfires. |
| **Thanksgiving Parades** | Fourth Thursday in November | Washington D.C., New York, Philadelphia | Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, National Christmas Tree lighting. |
| **Christmas Markets** | December | Various cities (e.g., Boston’s Faneuil Hall Market, San Francisco’s Union Square Holiday Market) | Seasonal crafts, holiday treats. |

These are just snapshots—you’ll find dozens more regional festivals ranging from county fair days to niche genre gatherings (indie rock, folk, electronic dance).

---

#### Quick Tips for Booking:

1. **Book Early:** Popular festivals fill up months in advance.  
2. **Check Accommodation Options:** Hotels near venues often price surge during peak times.  
3. **Look for Package Deals:** Some ticket vendors bundle lodging, transportation, and VIP perks.  
4. **Stay Flexible With Dates:** Off‑weekend tickets may be cheaper than Saturday/Sunday passes.  

Feel free to tell me a bit more about the kind of festival you’re interested in (music style, size, budget, travel distance), and I can narrow down recommendations even further!
